assistant.primaryUsageNote: The standard polite/formal way to thank someone in professional or respectful contexts. For casual peers use 고마워.

alternativeTranslations.note: Near-synonym of 감사합니다, slightly warmer in tone.
Strongly emphatic: use in written correspondence or formal speeches.
Highly deferential: appropriate for written thanks to superiors or customers.

senses.definition: An expression or feeling of gratitude.

assistant.etymology: From Middle English thankes, from Old English þancas, plural of þanc "thought, gratitude."
assistant.notes: Professional Korean correspondence typically uses 감사합니다 or 감사드립니다; 고맙습니다 is interchangeable but slightly less common in formal writing.
assistant.grammar: -합니다 is the 하십시오체 ending: highest politeness, used in professional and public speech.
